title: Threshold optimality, critical-lattice variance detection, and cross-scale rigidity for the Zeta23 rank-trace route

claims.statement: For 1 <= c <= 2, the simple-zero coefficient obtained from the same first and second moments is B_c(kappa)=1-(kappa-1)/(2c-1-c^2/2), which is maximized at c=2. Every nonnegative mixture of these scalar threshold inequalities is also bounded by 2-kappa.

The Schur-transfer defect has an exact rowwise Bregman decomposition and equality classification. For Q=0 and b=0, the full defect is the off-diagonal atom-Gram energy plus the squared atom-load excess above c.

For two compactly supported tapers on a common critical grid, the cross-Poisson kernel is independent of the lattice origin. Phase shifts, linear combinations, and Gram-level direct sums of same-scale tapers do not by themselves create new macroscopic scalar information.
claims.scope: full infinite common grid with the stated support and summability hypotheses
evidence: pinned Zeta23/Poisson.lean for the same-taper case

claims.statement: For a fixed-width smooth edge taper on an exact critical lattice, the normalized off-diagonal frame energy is O(w/L), so same-scale edge-profile optimization cannot create a fixed macroscopic gap as L tends to infinity.
claims.scope: exact critical lattice and bounded integer loads

claims.statement: In the ideal rectangular critical-lattice occupancy model with mean integer load one and the Zeta23 second-moment budget kappa(lambda)=1/lambda+lambda/3, lambda=3/4 forces variance at most 9/32, simple-load density at least 23/32, and occupied-cell density at least 55/64.

If the ideal critical-lattice simple-load density is at most 2/3, every relative scale lambda in ((sqrt(5)-1)/2,1) violates the corresponding second-moment budget by at least g(lambda)=(1-lambda)(lambda^2+lambda-1)/(3lambda^2); at lambda=3/4 the gap is 5/108.

The continuum of all rectangular scalar first/second-moment scale constraints cannot force a universal ideal-lattice simple-load density above 23/32: a half-frequency spectral extremizer of mass 9/32 is approached by integer alternating-block sequences.
claims.scope: ideal rectangular critical-lattice scalar spectral-measure model

claims.statement: For the period-six load pattern with four simple cells, one double cell and one vacancy, the best ideal cross-scale bound is approximately 0.721843050317375 at lambda approximately 0.728504383258803. This value is not arrangement-universal: an explicit period-twelve pattern has smaller defect at lambda=3/4.
For one isolated rectangular off-line reflection pair of multiplicity m and normalized depth y=L(beta-1/2), the pure c=2 defect is 4(m-1)^2+2m^2((sinh(y)/y)^2-1), at least 4(m-1)^2+(2/3)m^2y^2.
claims.scope: single isolated reflection pair in the ideal rectangular full-grid model

claims.statement: Under an a priori one-quarter-lattice displacement bound and loads at most two, the second-scale defect differs from its exact-lattice value by at most C times the square root of the first-scale defect, with a convergent explicit series for C. A coarse lambda=3/4 bound gives a positive conditional tradeoff margin above 2.2e-6.
claims.scope: periodic Kadec-neighborhood model with a priori matching

claims.statement: A uniform two-scale compactness gap should follow if zero first-scale defect forces a stationary local weak limit supported on one integer coset with marks at most two; the topology, intensity preservation and lower-semicontinuity steps remain open.
claims.scope: candidate inverse theorem for periodic marked configurations

claims.statement: At an exact critical lattice, fixed-width smooth Zeta23 tapers converge to the rectangular lattice symbol uniformly with error O(sqrt(w/L)) for load sequences with bounded second moment.
claims.scope: exact lattice; fixed relative scale; bounded second moment

heuristic_result.boundary: Finite-period coordinate search only; not global optimization and not proof.

validation.boundary: The deterministic harness verifies algebraic formulas, exact finite patterns and reproducible numerical scans. It does not verify the inverse theorem or any claim about actual zeta zeros.

correction_ledger.correction: The first draft scalar identity/sign in A-RH-RTD-0001 was corrected before that package was frozen.

The value 0.721843050317375 was initially a strong period-six signal, then explicitly downgraded after a period-twelve counterexample showed it is not arrangement-universal. The surviving universal ideal-model bound is 23/32.
The Q=0 full defect formula does not require the provisional extra hypothesis P <= cI; the exact load-excess term cancels the spectral-excess subtraction.

next_frontier.title: Two-scale sinc-rigidity / collapsed-lattice inverse theorem
next_frontier.statement: Derive, from o(N) genuine first-scale Zeta23 c=2 defect, an o(N)-loss decomposition into a common near-critical lattice of load-one cells, load-two tangent cells for on-line doubles or shallow simple off-line pairs, and a positive penalty for deep or multiple off-line pairs; then transfer the lambda=3/4 lattice symbol lower bound through the smooth taper, finite grid and tail matrix.
next_frontier.ideal_contradiction_if_simple_at_most_2_: 5/108 per unit multiplicity before stability losses

cannot_imply: The ideal critical-lattice bounds 23/32 and 55/64 are not unconditional theorems about Riemann-zeta zeros.
The period-six number 0.721843050317375 is not a universal bound.
The deterministic and jitter computations do not prove a stability or inverse theorem.
The single-pair depth formula does not control interacting collections of off-line pairs by itself.
No published zeta-zero proportion has been improved by this solver package.
This attempt does not prove or refute the Riemann hypothesis.
No claim is repository-verified before an isolated independent-verifier run returns PASS on the frozen artifact hashes.
